To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy consumption of an AP is a linear function of its activity time, that the energy consumption during the idle period can be ignored, and that the energy consumption in the sleep mode can be approximated by the energy consumption during idle periods.

1) the power model of the access points has a significant impact on the energy consumption of an IEEE 802.3af-based wireless LAN infrastructure, 2) the more detailed and accurate the power model, the slower the optimisation algorithms become, and 3) the most accurate models are rarely needed, as simpler and faster models can provide very good results.

i) the energy footprint of an enterprise wireless network can be substantially reduced by means of a network management solution that employs simple one- or two-component power models; and ii) the energy footprint reduction obtained with a detailed power model, while significant in some cases, is not substantial enough to justify the additional time required to solve the optimisation problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new power model that is accurate, yet simple enough to be used for the management of large-scale WLANs.
the trade-off between accuracy and efficiency in the energy management of large and midsize wireless LANs.

the design of energy-efficient wireless networks, but it has also a strong impact on the design of energy-aware network management tools, because it provides a set of guidelines on the selection and use of the power models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the energy-efficient management context, the use of simple models is preferable over more complex ones.
the power model should be chosen as simple as possible, while still providing a sufficiently accurate description of the power consumption of the APs.
the choice of the AP power models depends on the specific application and the available computing resources, rather than on the accuracy of the models themselves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AP power models can be simplified without compromising on the energy efficiency, thus reducing the complexity of the optimisation problem.
, in order to achieve the best trade-off between energy reduction and computational time, the AP power model should not be more complex than a two-component model.
, for energy management, the accuracy and complexity of the power model should be balanced against the time available for the solving process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the AP power models should not be driven only by the accuracy of the models, but also by the complexity of the optimisation problems to be solved.
, when designing a network management tool, one should carefully evaluate the trade-off between the accuracy of the model and the computational burden.
the energy optimisation of enterprise WLANs is a complex task, and the choice of the power model should not be taken for granted.
